blocks.title: Diffusion
blocks.md: **Diffusion** is the movement of particles from a place where there are many of them to a place where there are fewer, until they are spread evenly. It happens in gases and liquids and needs no energy. Oxygen enters cells and carbon dioxide leaves them by diffusion.

blocks.title: Osmosis
blocks.md: **Osmosis** is the movement of **water** through a **partially permeable membrane** from a **dilute solution** to a **concentrated solution**. A plant cell in pure water takes in water and becomes **turgid** (firm). In a strong solution it loses water and becomes **flaccid**; the plant wilts.

blocks.caption: Osmosis in a plant cell.
blocks.alt: Two boxes: with pure water outside the cell takes in water and becomes turgid; with a strong solution outside the cell loses water and becomes flaccid.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Osmosis is about *water* only; diffusion is about any particles.
- Water moves from the *dilute* to the *concentrated* solution.
- The membrane must be partially permeable.

blocks.title: Blood
blocks.md: Blood is made of **plasma** (the liquid, which carries food, urea, hormones and heat), **red blood cells** (carry oxygen with **haemoglobin**), **white blood cells** (fight germs) and **platelets** (help blood to clot). The heart pumps the blood round the **blood vessels**.

blocks.caption: The path of blood through the heart (the aorta leaves the left ventricle).
blocks.alt: Six boxes with arrows in order: body, right atrium, right ventricle, lungs, left atrium, left ventricle, then back to the body.

blocks.title: Heart and blood vessels
blocks.md:
The heart has four chambers: two **atria** (receive blood) and two **ventricles** (pump blood out). The **left ventricle** has the thickest wall because it pumps blood all round the body. **Valves** stop blood going backwards.

- **Arteries**: carry blood away from the heart; thick walls.
- **Veins**: carry blood to the heart; have valves.
- **Capillaries**: very thin; where substances pass between blood and cells.

blocks.title: Looking after your heart (flag for health review)
blocks.md: Regular exercise, a balanced diet without too much fat and salt, and not smoking help keep the heart healthy. Your **pulse** (felt at the wrist) shows how many times the heart beats each minute; it rises during exercise.

blocks.title: Pulse in an hour
blocks.statement: A resting heart beats 72 times per minute. How many beats in one hour?

blocks.title: Which vessel?
blocks.statement: A vessel with thick walls carries blood from the heart to the body. What is it called, and which chamber does the blood come from?
steps: Thick walls and carrying blood away from the heart: an artery.
Blood to the body leaves the left ventricle through the aorta.
blocks.answer: An artery (the aorta) from the left ventricle
